title: Adaptations: built to survive
subject: science
strengths: Most of the class can name the cactus features and say what each one does.
The class can explain camouflage and why birds migrate.

modelAnswers.question: Winter is coming and food is getting hard to find. What do some birds do, and why?
modelAnswers.answer: The birds migrate: when winter comes and food is hard to find, they fly thousands of kilometres to warmer places, and return when spring brings food back.

modelAnswers.question: Name two features that help a cactus survive in the hot, dry desert and say what each one does.
modelAnswers.answer: Its thick stem stores water like a bottle, its sharp thorns stop thirsty animals from biting it, and its deep roots reach down to find water.

commonErrors.misconception: An animal can decide to grow a new feature when it needs one.
commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that the cactus grew thorns because it decided it needed them.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: say how the cactus's features really came to be, and over how long.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: the features did not appear overnight - they developed over many, many generations, not by choice.

commonErrors.misconception: An animal can decide to grow a new feature when it needs one.
commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner says an animal grew a helpful feature because it decided it needed one.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: rewrite the sentence so the feature develops over generations instead of being chosen.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: no living thing chooses its features - they developed over many, many generations, not by choice.
